name: Diotimus of Athens
bio: Diotimus of Athens is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors gives no date for the poet. Paton's index lists the poet among the writers of Meleager's Wreath, the Garland compiled about 100 BC.
This archive carries the 1 epigram ascribed to the poet in the second volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Book VII: 420).

poems.title: Book VII, 420
poems.author: Diotimus of Athens
poems.text: Ye Hopes of men, light goddesses—for never, were ye not so, had Hades, who bringeth our strength to naught, covered Lesbon, once as blest as the Great King—yea, ye Hopes and ye Loves too, lightest of all deities, farewell! And ye, the flutes he once breathed in must lie dumb and unheard; for Acheron knoweth no troops of musicians. The city of Cos, to distinguish it from an earlier capital of the island, was known as Cos Meropis.
